page: Amazon Web Services vt1.3xlarge is a specialized accelerated computing instance designed primarily for real-time video transcoding and media processing workflows. Driven by the AWS Nitro System hypervisor, the virtual machine features 12 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 6 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The CPU architecture supports x86_64 instruction sets including AVX-512 extensions. Memory is provisioned with 24 GB of DDR4 system RAM operating at 3 GHz, delivering 2.0 GB per vCPU.

Hardware acceleration is provided by a single Xilinx U30 media accelerator equipped with 24 GB of dedicated VRAM. The instance carries no local NVMe storage, requiring network-attached storage via Amazon EBS, and provides a baseline network throughput of 3 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Synthetic CPU evaluations place the platform in average bands for general multi-threaded compute, scoring 10,911.36 on PassMark CPU and 5,969.0 on Geekbench multi-core, while single-threaded tasks register lower relative marks, such as 1,324.09 on stress-ng.

Memory bandwidth benchmarks demonstrate consistent performance, yielding 72.07 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 44.54 GB/sec for write tasks. Workloads that focus on general-purpose machine learning or text compression underperform relative to modern general compute, with 7B parameter LLM inference showing poor prompt processing rates of 14.1 tokens/sec. Consequently, the vt1.3xlarge delivers cost-efficient performance primarily when leveraging its integrated Xilinx ASIC for high-density video streaming, live encoding, and OTT broadcasting pipelines rather than standard CPU-bound enterprise jobs.
description: Amazon Web Services vt1.3xlarge is an accelerated computing instance engineered for video transcoding and media pipeline processing. It features 12 vCPUs across 6 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 2.5 GHz, paired with 24 GB of DDR4 system memory. Hardware acceleration is provided by a dedicated Xilinx U30 card featuring 24 GB of VRAM. The instance relies entirely on remote storage, containing no local disks, and operates on a 3 Gbps baseline network interface via the AWS Nitro System. Benchmark metrics highlight mid-tier multi-core processor performance and DDR4 memory throughput, alongside weak CPU-based compression and large language model inference speeds. Cost efficiency is optimized strictly for media-centric workloads that take direct advantage of the specialized Xilinx ASIC hardware, making the instance suitable for live video transcoding, adaptive bitrate streaming, and multi-channel video distribution.
